failure_modes: One passage is a researcher/host generalising about what OTHER experiencers report ('The description I hear the most on people coming back... being slammed back into my body')
One passage is a repeatable self-induced out-of-body experience during a nap, not the NDE re-entry

best_quote.text: I felt myself suddenly and violently yanked back into my body, which was still about 40 feet away, in the back bedroom - WHOOSH!

failure_modes: 'I didn't believe' used in a non-atheism sense — disbelieving a reiki teacher, disbelieving psychics while still nominally Catholic
Loss of faith AFTER the event ('I didn't believe in God anymore after the accident'), which is the inverse of the claim
Speakers who explicitly deny being atheist ('I wouldn't say I was atheist, per se') still match
Disbelief located in teenage years with no link to belief-state at the time of the NDE
audits.suggested_regex: \b(?:was|were|had been|used to be)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:militant\s+|total\s+|complete\s+|closet\s+|feverishly\s+)?(?:atheist|agnostic)\b|\bI (?:didn't|did not) believe in (?:God|an afterlife|any afterlife|life after death)\b(?!\s*anymore)

best_quote.text: I didn't believe in God, but it was like I met God.

failure_modes: The hospital whirlpool bath in the physiotherapy department (two near-duplicate passages) — a literal medical whirlpool, not a passage
Life-story metaphor: 'I kept spiraling further downhill', 'my health spiraled down very fast'
'vortex of the child welfare system' — pure figure of speech from an unrelated narrative
Swirling things that are not passages: colours swirled through God's throne, a whirling mist visitation, a swirling hourglass of light seen at a distance
Swirl at the moment of exit in a meditation-induced OBE, not an NDE transit

best_quote.text: the tunnel sort of twisted and it corkscrewed. So there was movement. It wasn't just static like turning around me. It was turning and moving at the same time

failure_modes: The exact inversion: 'they were going to send me back to where I came from' / 'I turned around to go back where I came from' — here 'where I came from' means Earth or a direction in space, not the origin
Post-hoc sermon and affirmation material ('our true home is in the spiritual world', 'that's where we came from, we came here with free will') — general cosmology, not a perception
A poem read aloud from a book about returning 'to where we all come from'
Untranslatable philosophical rambling where 'we came from there' is a rhetorical aside

best_quote.text: Then, with a sudden burst of joy, I realized that this was my real home. Back on Earth, I had been a visitor, a misfit, and a homesick stranger.

failure_modes: Physical-world noise at the moment of injury: the sound of the car crash, the noise of a sandstorm

Sounds heard INSIDE the destination rather than during the crossing — humming from trees, light beams that buzz as they pass through the head (two passages), whale-song and wind-chime sounds of other worlds
Generalised instruction about what one 'may hear' during separation — a teaching, not a report
'whoosh' as a narrative sound effect in biography (an entity stepping in to defend the body)
A roaring sound as a lingering post-NDE aftereffect days later, not at the crossing
audits.suggested_regex: \b(?:whoosh(?:ing)?|roar(?:ing)?|rushing|buzz(?:ing)?|humming|whirring|ringing|hiss(?:ing)?)\b[^.]{0,90}\b(?:out of (?:my|the) body|left my body|leave my body|tunnel|back into my body|the other side|separat\w+)\b|\b(?:out of my body|left my body|tunnel|back into my body|other side)\b[^.]{0,90}\b(?:whoosh(?:ing)?|roaring|rushing sound|buzz(?:ing)? (?:sound|noise)|humming|whirring|ringing in my ears)\b

best_quote.text: I "heard" a loud buzzing sound and also a "rushing" sound, like Niagara Falls. Suddenly, I found myself outside my body and beside my bed

failure_modes: Ordinary parenting and biography: custody battles, a child born with Down syndrome, 'my children really needed somebody to help take care of them' while she was ill
'my kids need me' shouted in the hospital room to get a doctor's attention — the medical setting, not the other side
Two near-duplicate OBE passages where 'my kids need me' only explains why she habitually checks the clock
Advice to paramedics that they should say 'your children need you' at a resuscitation — speculation about others
Channel boilerplate (Instagram/website sign-off) that happens to mention 'my kids'
audits.suggested_regex: \b(?:go(?:ing)? back|come back|return(?:ing)?|not my time|leave them)\b[^.]{0,120}\bmy (?:son|daughter|kids|children|baby|babies|boys|girls)\b|\bmy (?:son|daughter|kids|children|baby|babies|boys|girls)\b[^.]{0,60}\bneed(?:s|ed)? me\b[^.]{0,120}\b(?:go back|come back|return|can't stay|couldn't stay|have to go)\b

best_quote.text: I wanted to go back for my children. I knew deep down they needed me and nothing was going to stop me from getting back to them.

failure_modes: Theological debate about whether one is OBLIGED to dissolve back into Source — free-will commentary, hypothetical and future-tense ('if you want to merge with source, you can'), two passages from the same speaker
The interviewer's own question ('can you focus on the mechanics of the merger?') and a host reading from the guest's book
Observing OTHER souls already merged with God rather than being absorbed oneself (two passages)
Meditation/stillness talk about 'becoming one with everything', and a YouTube-channel plug about 'the whole idea of enlightenment and merging with God'
audits.suggested_regex: \bI (?:was|got) (?:absorbed|dissolved|melted|drawn|taken) into\b|\bI (?:merged|dissolved|melted|blended) (?:with|into)\b|\bI became (?:one with|part of) (?:the|that|this) (?:light|love|oneness)\b|\bmerged with (?:the|this|that) light\b

best_quote.text: I plunged, plunged into it and merged, and merged with this light. At which point, everything changed. My personal sense of identity was gone at that point. I was this light.

failure_modes: 'group of souls' used for reincarnation soul-group philosophy ('the same thousand or 10,000 will come back into your life in lifetimes') rather than a perceived crowd
Small councils of three, four or twelve beings — structurally the opposite of the mass the claim describes
A channelled entity ('still heirlam speaking') lecturing about what happens when 'a group of souls' works with dark intention
A psychic telling the guest he is 'protected by thousands of angels right now', plus a book plug
Two duplicate passages where the group is eight shadowed figures in a hospital hallway
New-age oversoul/fractal theorising where 'group of beings' means humanity

best_quote.text: On the other side of the river were hundreds of souls, and I knew that during many lifetimes I had lived and interacted with them.

failure_modes: Podcast and radio boilerplate — host intros, 'link in the description', episode teasers that list 'visions of possible future events' (four passages)
A YouTube narrator analysing somebody ELSE's NDE and its predictions
A researcher's statistical aside: 'of the 1200 testimonies I've heard, a very small percentage are shown future events'
Precognitive dreams in ordinary life and future-seeing in a past-life regression — not the NDE
'our perception of future events' used in a general talk about which emotions survive death
audits.suggested_regex: \bI (?:was|am) (?:being )?shown\b[^.]{0,80}\b(?:future|what (?:was|would be) coming|their lives|my life)\b|\b(?:they|he|she|it) showed me\b[^.]{0,60}\b(?:future|what would happen)\b|\blife preview\b|\bI saw (?:my|the) future\b

best_quote.text: Then they showed me through the same screen some future events in my life if I chose to return to it. Some events would definitely occur, and some events were possible but not definite.

failure_modes: The single biggest contaminant: the blood-pressure free-fall sensation on the gurney — 'imagine jumping out of an airplane without a parachute' while nurses call out 50 over 15. FOUR near-identical passages, all the same story, all the medical setting
'I fell into a deep depression' / 'a deep hole' / 'a deep peaceful sleep' — biography and idiom (four passages)
'I kind of chose to just freefall' as a life-choice metaphor, and a preacher's 'fallen into the pit of feeling you've gone too far'
Physical collapse on a bathroom floor from hypoxia, and a blow to the temple that 'plunged me into darkness' (loss of consciousness)
A host recounting other people's glimpses of a bottomless pit

best_quote.text: the bottom dropped out, just like you're in an elevator and the floor opens up and you start falling into total darkness. And the thought came, there is a hell.

failure_modes: 'pearly gates' invoked as the cliche being DENIED — 'it wasn't the pearly gates either', 'I had always understood heaven is pearly gates, streets of gold. It wasn't anything like that' (four passages of expectation or negation)
Ordinary gates: an airport departure gate, a log-cabin gate left open, a house gate in a Portuguese biography, the gates of a temple on Sunset Boulevard
Doctrine and book titles — 'Jesus died to open the gates of heaven for all mankind', the memoir 'From Vegas to the Pearly Gates'
The interviewer generalising about experiences 'at the gates of heaven'
A childhood sky-vision of golden gates at age 11, outside any NDE
audits.suggested_regex: \b(?:saw|reached|approached|came to|stood (?:at|before)|was (?:taken|brought|led) to|went through|walked through|entered|circled)\b[^.]{0,60}\b(?:gates? of heaven|heaven'?s gates?|the gates?|a gate)\b(?![^.]{0,30}(?:security|flight|airport|boarding))

best_quote.text: While at heaven's gate, which was closed, I saw myself alone before the gate. Then a man opened the gate for me

failure_modes: 'they were waiting for me' in the hospital sense — the surgical team waiting, twelve staff at the ER door, family waiting in the waiting room (three passages)
A speaker describing a CHILD's case in the third person ('that was his greeting committee for his pets')
Biography: demonic presences that 'knew I was coming and were waiting for me' in a Texas town
A promise of a FUTURE greeting ('they would all be there to greet me when it was time') rather than an arrival
A single welcomer or a disembodied welcoming voice, where the claim is specifically about an assembled group
audits.suggested_regex: \b(?:welcom(?:e|ing) (?:committee|party)|greeting committee|(?:they|we)re waiting for me|were (?:there )?(?:waiting for|to greet) me|greeted me|welcomed me home)\b(?![^.]{0,60}(?:hospital|waiting room|surgery|surgical|doctors|nurses|emergency))

best_quote.text: And everyone envelops me in this huge hug. There's 18 or 20 souls there. It's my soul family.

failure_modes: 'abyss' as pure metaphor: the abyss of grief and bereavement, a black hole of abyss meaning depression, 'the abyss of God's wisdom', 'the abyss of humanity's existence in the Holocaust', a 'weekend abyss' spent nursing a dying partner (six passages)
'chasm' meaning emotional distance from a son, or an 'emotional chasm of stuff' unwound by Jesus
'abyss' meaning benign cosmic vastness — staring down into galaxies and nebulas with awe and no fear (three near-duplicate passages from the same account)
Hosts and interviewers talking about 'the pit of hell' with Bible quotation attached
A speaker retelling another woman's NDE across a chasm
audits.suggested_regex: \b(?:teetering|standing|stood|edge of|brink of|looked down|fall(?:ing)?|fell)\b[^.]{0,60}\b(?:bottomless pit|black pit|dark pit|the pit|the abyss(?! of (?:grief|God|humanity|despair)))\b|\b(?:bottomless pit|black pit|the abyss)\b[^.]{0,60}\b(?:no bottom|never climb|fall(?: in| into| down)?|darker than)\b

best_quote.text: So I was teetering over the edge of a black pit. And in front of me was a darkness.

failure_modes: 'not allowed' in ordinary life — a restraining order, a teenage girlfriend he 'wasn't allowed to see', a psychologist's account of being sixteen and 'not allowed to pursue it', spirits 'not allowed to come to me' when off duty

'couldn't get past' as idiom or physical obstruction — firemen and a gurney, a doctor's belly button, a rope jammed on a rock ledge, veterans who 'can't get past things', a host's 'I can't get beyond the fact that...'
The dying body failing physically ('I couldn't get past my knees'), which is the medical setting not a boundary in the realm
Third-party generalisation about NDEs — 'people are only allowed to visit the entrance, they are not allowed to continue in'
Boundaries reported for OTHER souls in a mediumship context, and one meditation vision rather than an NDE
audits.suggested_regex: \bI (?:couldn't|could not|wasn't allowed to|was not allowed to|was not permitted to|knew I couldn't)\s(?:go|move|proceed|continue|cross|pass|travel)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(?:any (?:further|farther)|further|beyond|past (?:this|that))\b|\bthis (?:was|is) as far as I (?:could go|got)\b

best_quote.text: I was aware that somehow there were unseen barriers beyond which I knew I was not permitted to pass.
